blocks.text: Carboxylic acids are organic compounds with the carboxyl functional group, -COOH; the general formula is RCOOH. Common examples are methanoic acid (formic acid, found in ants), ethanoic acid (acetic acid, in vinegar) and butanoic acid (butyric acid, in rancid butter).

The lower carboxylic acids are liquids at room temperature with high boiling points, because their molecules form hydrogen bonds; ethanoic acid molecules pair up as hydrogen-bonded dimers. Ethanoic acid melts at 17 C and boils at 118 C. Its melting point is close to room temperature, so it solidifies in winter; the solid form of pure ethanoic acid is called glacial acetic acid because it looks like a glacier. Because they form hydrogen bonds with water, the lower acids, methanoic and ethanoic acid, are soluble in water.

blocks.alt: Left: the carboxyl group, a carbon with a C=O and an -OH, and R. Right: two ethanoic acid molecules facing each other, joined by two dashed hydrogen bonds from the C=O oxygen of each to the O-H of the other.
blocks.caption: The carboxyl group and the hydrogen-bonded dimer of ethanoic acid (original diagram after the book's dimer).
blocks.long_description: The carboxyl group combines a carbonyl group and a hydroxyl group on the same carbon. The O-H hydrogen of one molecule is attracted to the C=O oxygen of another, so two molecules hold each other by two hydrogen bonds; extra energy is needed to separate them, giving a high boiling point.

blocks.text: Long-chain aliphatic monocarboxylic acids are called fatty acids. Stearic, palmitic and oleic acids are found in vegetable oils as triglycerides; palmitic acid, C16H32O2, occurs in large amounts in palm oil. Fatty acids are insoluble in water because of their long hydrophobic (water-repelling) alkyl chains.

blocks.prompt: Why does ethanoic acid have a much higher boiling point than ethanal?
blocks.explanation: Ethanoic acid molecules form hydrogen bonds (dimers) through their -OH and C=O groups; ethanal has no O-H and cannot hydrogen-bond to itself.

items: Carboxylic acids: RCOOH; e.g. methanoic, ethanoic, butanoic acids.
Hydrogen-bonded dimers: high boiling points; small acids dissolve in water.
Fatty acids: long chains, insoluble in water.
